body.statement: For every \(I\in\mathfrak J_q^{\mathrm{nw}}\) and equality factor \(H\), a feasible \(x_H\in K_H\) is extreme if and only if the columns of \(A_H\) indexed by its positive support are linearly independent. The support construction defining \(\mathcal V_H\) therefore satisfies \(\mathcal V_H=\operatorname{ext}(K_H)\), contains at most \(2^{|H|}\) rational vectors, and every numerator and denominator in every listed vector has binary encoding length \(O(B^2)\). The same conclusions hold for each \(K_c\); in particular, rationality and the encoding-length bound are established before any endpoint theorem invokes vertex enumeration or elimination.
body.justification: This separates rational vertex existence and bit growth from the later optimization theorem instead of smuggling them into an undefined use of \(\operatorname{ext}\).
body.gap: Standard rational-polyhedron facts do not by themselves certify that the serialized support list is exhaustive or quantify its coordinate encoding under this canonical input measure.
body.consumer: The generator and skeptical verifier obtain an exact finite rational domain with an explicit per-coordinate bit budget.
